CHAPTER III
ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS
Air Quality
A haul road of 4.5 miles in length covering approximately 136 acres is assumed in order to deliver coal from Tract II to the Tract III facilities. Also, portions of the county road will undergo relocation on both tracts as mining progresses. Based on the results of a study conducted in the early 1970's under the auspices of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA, 1973) the average particulate loading at a typical road construction site was estimated to be one to two tons per acre per month during all phases of activity. Actual rates of emission due to construction of the haul road and relocation of the county road will be dependent on the rate of construction, number and type of construction vehicles involved, time of year, soil types, etc.
Emission rates of various effluents from light-duty gasolinepowered trucks, and heavy duty diesel and gasoline-powered construction\nequipment have been determined by the U.S. EPA (1976). Based on these\nemission rates and on the numbers of major equipment required, it is\nestimated that approximately 100 grams per second of nitrogen oxides
(the most abundant gaseous emission by far from heavy-duty dieselpowered vehicles) would be emitted to the atmosphere under the most
probable coal development scenario. This amount is not considered to
result in an adverse impact on the air quality of the site vicinity,
because of numerous individual sources which are spread out over several
thousand acres.
